text.name: Saved Remote Desktop passwords
text.titlePass: Remote Desktop does not save passwords
text.why: A saved Remote Desktop password lets anyone at this PC, or malware on it, open the remote computer.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc and search Administrative Templates for Remote Desktop Connection Client.
Enable "Do not allow passwords to be saved".

registry.item: Saving of Remote Desktop passwords blocked

absent.found: Not configured (Windows default: passwords can be saved)

text.name: Remote Assistance
text.why: Remote Assistance lets someone you invite see and control your screen. Scammers talk people into sending that invitation.
fix: Press Windows+R, type SystemPropertiesRemote and press Enter.
Clear "Allow Remote Assistance connections to this computer" and select OK.
If the box is greyed out, the setting comes from your organisation: tell IT.

text.name: WinRM client: Basic sign-in
text.titlePass: Remote management never sends passwords as plain text
text.titleFail: Remote management may send passwords as plain text
text.why: Basic sign-in sends the password itself to the other computer, readable by anyone who can watch the connection.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc and search Administrative Templates for Windows Remote Management (WinRM) > WinRM Client.
Disable "Allow Basic authentication".

text.name: WinRM client: unencrypted traffic
text.titlePass: Remote management from this PC is always encrypted
text.titleFail: Remote management from this PC may be unencrypted
text.why: Unencrypted remote management shows commands, and whatever they return, to anyone who can watch the network.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc and search Administrative Templates for Windows Remote Management (WinRM) > WinRM Client.
Disable "Allow unencrypted traffic".

text.name: WinRM service: Basic sign-in
text.titlePass: This PC refuses plain-text passwords for remote management
text.titleFail: This PC accepts plain-text passwords for remote management
text.why: Basic sign-in sends the password itself over the network, readable by anyone who can watch the connection.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc and search Administrative Templates for Windows Remote Management (WinRM) > WinRM Service.
Disable "Allow Basic authentication".

text.name: WinRM service: unencrypted traffic
text.titlePass: Remote management of this PC is always encrypted
text.titleFail: Remote management of this PC may be unencrypted
text.why: Unencrypted remote management shows commands, and whatever they return, to anyone who can watch the network.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc and search Administrative Templates for Windows Remote Management (WinRM) > WinRM Service.
Disable "Allow unencrypted traffic".

text.name: Remote Registry service
text.titlePass: The Remote Registry service is disabled
text.titleFail: The Remote Registry service is not disabled
text.why: Remote Registry lets other computers read and change this PC's settings over the network. A staff PC does not need it.
fix: Press Windows+R, type services.msc and press Enter.
Open Remote Registry, select Stop, set Startup type to Disabled and select OK.
If a management tool needs the service, tell IT instead.
